title: Release quest-cli 0.13.0, paired with lore 0.13.0, so the opum-quest plugin ships the Quest board mod
description:
Operator instruction, 2026-10-02 (relayed by opum-doc as ODOC-OP-2026-10-02-10; tracked in opum-agent as OPAG-1074): ship the Quest board in the opum-quest plugin. QCLI-431 builds the mod and lands it on dev; this task releases it, because the plugin is cut from this repository at the CLI's own tag -- plugin users get the board only once a release carries it, and the marketplace pin moves to that release.

VERSION: 0.12.0 is published for both quest and lore. The mod is a new feature, so the next shared number is 0.13.0; lore-cli bumps to the same number under the pair rule (constitution Article 3, the shape QCLI-421 recorded for 0.12.0). Sequencing the pair is opum-agent's call, not this task's -- if the pair moves differently, this title and these criteria move with it.

Established already, so the release does not re-derive it:
- The publish parity gate refuses a quest publish until lore-cli's MAIN reads the same version. Measure it with the gate's own --require rather than assuming, before planning the pair.
- Publication is tier 3 and runs only on the operator's own authorization, given in this session's dialog. Nothing in this task authorizes a publish by itself.
- quest-web's link gate fetches every external link it renders and cites this repository's release tag for its own release.version. A new tag is additive and safe; moving or deleting an existing tag is not, and needs quest-web told first.
- The board mod's changelog entry did not land with QCLI-431 (its criteria do not cover one). The 0.11.0 release commit recorded the plugin-detection change the same way (QCLI-387), so recording it here is the established shape, and it is an explicit criterion below rather than a hope.

PRECEDENT: QCLI-421 (the 0.12.0 bump -- every version site, the six platform packages, the managed block, the changelog) and docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, whose eight steps this task follows.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every hand-edited version site reads 0.13.0: package.json .version and its six optionalDependencies pins, QUEST_VERSION, QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION, the conformance fixture questVersion, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the six platform manifests; bun.lock's six pins are regenerated by bun install under the pinned bun 1.4.2. The site count is reported from a grep rather than remembered.

All six platform packages are rebuilt at 0.13.0 with the pinned bun 1.4.2 and committed, with each platform manifest's questBinarySha256 and the root's questPlatformPackages regenerated; check:packages and check:lockfile exit 0.
CHANGELOG.md names the Quest board mod as a consumer-observable change in the 0.13.0 section, under a fresh empty Unreleased heading, and the v0.13.0 tag carries that edit rather than a later commit.
The native-execution receipt for the tagged commit passes bun run receipt:require, and receipt:verify-published compares the registry's six platform tarballs to it after publication.

No publish step runs before lore-cli's main reads the same version and the operator has authorized publication in this session's dialog, and the publish STAGES under release-candidate rather than moving latest.

The opum-quest plugin cut from v0.13.0 validates with the board module present (claude plugin validate on the tagged tree), and the marketplace pin move to v0.13.0 is confirmed by the session that owns it.

The bump, platform packages, changelog, tag, receipt and publication result land on dev by squash merge with every required check a completed success on the exact head SHA, and dev is fast-forwarded to main.

plan: Claim QCLI-433, record this plan, and land both by squash merge before the bump work starts: a status change is a deliberate tracker write and takes its own branch and PR.

Strings commit on chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0. Move to 0.13.0: package.json .version and its six optionalDependencies pins, src/application/version.ts QUEST_VERSION, src/contract/tracker/index.ts QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION, fixtures/tracker/v1/conformance.json questVersion, .claude-plugin/plugin.json .version, and each npm/quest-<platform>/package.json .version. Leave the binaries, each questBinarySha256 and root questPlatformPackages untouched, so the checksum half of check:packages still passes while the version half reads the new number. Regenerate bun.lock's six pins with bun install under the pinned 1.4.2. check:packages and check:lockfile exit 0 in this state.

CHANGELOG.md gains the board mod's consumer-observable entry under ## Unreleased. The Unreleased -> 0.13.0 rename and its fresh successor heading are tag-time steps (runbook step 5) and are deliberately left undone here.

Bytes: with source-gates green on the strings head, dispatch prepublication-qualification.yml against the branch, collect the quest-package-<target> artifacts from immutable-candidates, and commit the six binaries with their regenerated manifests and checksums. The local build:packages route is not taken on this host: it risks the darwin-arm64 code-signing hazard the runbook records.
Regenerate CLAUDE.md's managed Quest block with the freshly built darwin-arm64 binary from those artifacts rather than the global install, and confirm quest agents --check reports current.

Verify on the final head: bun run check under the pinned bun 1.4.2, check:packages, check:lockfile, check:breaking-bump --pair --lore-ref dev --next 0.13.0, and lore check. Land by squash merge with every required check a completed success on the exact head SHA.
Tier 3, left to the operator in this session's own dialog: the tag, the native-execution receipt, the publish, and verify-published. This task's work tags, stages and publishes nothing.
implementationNotes:
BOUNDARY ON QCLI-433, 2026-10-02, second session, reached on an orchestrator-directed context budget. State at writing, read live.

READY AND PUSHED, awaiting one gate. Branch chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0 at 7f567a67; PR opum-ai/quest-cli#486 open against dev, non-draft, MERGEABLE. Three commits: 44abe989 version strings; 945ee3f2 the changelog entry; 7f567a67 the CI-built platform binaries with their regenerated manifests, the root checksum map, and CLAUDE.md's managed block at 0.13.0.

THE ONE RED, and it is not a defect in this work. lore check fails on the pair-version requirement: "the lore 0.12.0 / quest 0.13.0 pair version requirement is not met: lore 0.12.0 requires quest 0.12.0", exit 6. .github/workflows/lore-check.yml line 159 hardcodes `npm install -g @opum-ai/lore@0.12.0`, so the job cannot install the lore a quest 0.13.0 tree requires. Tracker integrity is success on the same head. The PR cannot go green until lore 0.13.0 exists on npm AND that pin moves; the ordering of that pair is a sequencing decision to route, not one to take here (operator instruction 2026-10-02, opum-agent OPAG-1086). If the pin move belongs in this PR rather than a follow-up, that is the question to answer.

VERIFIED LOCALLY on the bytes head, each measured rather than assumed: check:packages exit 0; check:lockfile 6 of 6; test:packages exit 0; all six binary digests computed by hand and matching both their manifests and the root map, 6/6; check:breaking-bump --next 0.13.0 exit 0 and its --pair form reading lore-cli@dev dab213522174e11b98029ad72b008925be9dd4e5 exit 0, both sides minor with no breaking heading; quest agents --check --target claude reports current.

HOW THE BYTES WERE OBTAINED. prepublication-qualification run 37073166852 dispatched against the branch; all six targets green plus source-gates and candidate-bundle. That route rather than a local build because bun cannot cross-compile win32-arm64, and a local macOS build additionally risks the darwin-arm64 code-signing hazard the runbook records. Each npm/quest-<target> was replaced wholesale from its artifact, so the regenerated manifest and its questBinarySha256 arrive with the binary, and root questPlatformPackages takes those same digests. The managed block was regenerated by EXECUTING THE ARTIFACT COPY under /tmp, never the in-repo binary, and the in-repo binary was then recreated from the untouched artifact, so the committed path is a fresh unexecuted vnode and git never had to survive the taint. Two side effects a successor should not mistake for defects: the win32 binaries' mode moved 755 -> 644, which is the mode the Windows runners upload and the generator deliberately does not chmod, and the push carries GitHub's large-file warnings for the six 60-83 MB binaries, as every prior release does.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the Unreleased -> 0.13.0 changelog rename (tag time, runbook step 5), the tag, the native-execution receipt, the publish, receipt:verify-published, and the dev-to-main promotion. Nothing is tagged, staged, published or promoted.

ALSO OPEN, ADJACENT: the board build choices (the across-refs toggle, repository discovery through userConfig, the uncommitted-window banner, and the Reference layout) are under opum-doc review and must not change while it runs.

WHAT THE SUCCESSOR SHOULD REACH FOR: the opum-sdlc skill before any branch or merge work, the release runbook docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md for the tag-time steps, and opum-quest for tracker writes. The six artifacts are still at /tmp/qcli433-artifacts if the bytes need re-deriving; they expire with the run's 7-day retention.

FULL CHECK, measured after the boundary note above was written: bun run check under the pinned bun 1.4.2 exits 0 on the bytes head 7f567a67 -- repository suite 1076 pass / 0 fail across 121 files, mod suite 14 pass / 0 fail across 3 files. So the local evidence for that head is the package gates, the six hand-computed digests, the breaking-bump pair check, and the repository's own full suite; the single red remains lore check on the pair-version requirement, which is the workflow's lore 0.12.0 pin and not this work.
